segments.text: Euclid's Elements. Book One, Proposition One. Given a finite segment A B, construct an equilateral triangle A B C upon it.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements. Book One, Proposition One. Given a finite segment A B,
construct an equilateral triangle A B C upon it.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: With center A and radius A B, describe circle A B. With center B and radius B A, describe circle B A. Mark point C where the two circles intersect, and join segments C A and C B.

subsegments.text: With center A and radius A B, describe circle A B.
With center B and radius B A, describe circle B A.
Mark point C where the two circles intersect,
and join segments C A and C B.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Since A is the center of circle A B, segment A C equals segment A B. Since B is the center of circle B A, segment B C also equals segment B A. Things equal to the same thing are equal to one another, so A C, A B, and B C are all equal. Therefore triangle A B C is equilateral, constructed on the given segment A B, as was required to do.
